summary: Backend-only testing of new user profile persistence (POST /api/users, GET /api/users/{phone}) plus regression on existing endpoints. 16/16 pytest cases pass on localhost:8001.

minor.issue: Returns HTTP 200 on create; conventionally a resource creation should return 201. Not a bug — upsert semantics make 200 reasonable — flag only.

There is no DB unique index on the 'phone' field of the users collection. Two concurrent POSTs for the same new phone could race and insert duplicate docs. Recommend creating a unique index: db.users.create_index('phone', unique=True).

action_items: (Optional) Return 201 from POST /api/users on first create vs 200 on update for clearer semantics.
(Optional) Add a unique index on users.phone in MongoDB at startup to prevent race-condition duplicates.

(Optional) The /api/auth/verify-token endpoint also upserts users with empty name/company on first verification — this means a GET /api/users/{phone} immediately after OTP verify will return a profile with name=''. Frontend already handles this by treating empty-name docs as 'not yet onboarded', but consider making GET return 404 when name is empty so the existing-profile-restore logic in index.tsx is simpler.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~600 lines and mixes user profile, loads, geocode, places, shortener, firebase auth — consider splitting into routers/{users,loads,geo,shorten,auth}.py for maintainability.
_norm_phone trims only the trailing 10 digits — good for +91/91 prefixes, but it will silently truncate a 12-digit non-Indian number. Acceptable since this is an India-only app, but worth a comment.

verify-token endpoint upserts user with empty name/company; combined with GET /api/users/{phone} returning 200 on that empty doc, this slightly contradicts the 'restore profile only if it exists' contract. The frontend currently guards via name length, but it is a subtle coupling.

No rate limiting on POST /api/users — anyone with a phone number can overwrite the name/company tied to that phone (no auth required). For production, this endpoint should be gated by a verified Firebase id_token so only the owner of the phone can edit its profile.
Mongo _id is correctly excluded via projection {'_id': 0} — good.
seed_data_creation: Test creates and cleans up users with phones 9876543210, 9876543211, 9000000099, 9000000088 and a TEST_ load row (deleted after test).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend was tested against http://localhost:8001 because frontend/.env points to a separate prod Render deployment (EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL=https://ptl-market.onrender.com). Reuse /app/backend/tests/test_users_api.py for regression — it covers POST /api/users (create/upsert/normalisation/validation), GET /api/users/{phone} (200/404/400), Mongo persistence, and basic regression on /api/, /api/pincode, /api/loads, /api/auth/verify-token. Firebase Admin is NOT initialised in this preview pod (no service-account env vars), so verify-token returns 500 for any token — only assert the endpoint exists.
rca of the issue: Original problem: backend did not persist user profile; only Firebase OTP verification existed. Main agent added UserProfile model, POST /api/users (upsert keyed by 10-digit normalised phone) and GET /api/users/{phone}, plus an upsert side-effect in /api/auth/verify-token. All flows verified working end-to-end against MongoDB.
